text:
mara: Heads-up — saw a sustained tail on p99 for tenant 'winch' in eu-west-1 over the last 6h, spikes correlate with large embedding jobs + a ~3x egress burst. graphs: https://grafana.company/redwood/d/egress
jon: saw it, looks like their KV-cache regen is thrashing our shared slab. p50 fine, p99 jumps when slab recycling fires.
sasha: any chance we can move them to a shield lane (short lived) while we triage? avoids dedicated reservation.
vik: shield lanes are fine but need a controlled window so we don't starve other short jobs. thinking: egress-windowing + soft-preempt for heavy allocs.
mara: proposal: 10m micro-quarantine for allocs > 8 GPUs or egress > 200MB/s sustained, with a soft-preempt backoff of 2x.
jon: can we implement as a routing policy? config snippet I used before:
```
route:
  - match: tenant.winches
    action: shield-window
    params: {max_duration: "10m", egress_threshold_mb: "200"}
```
chen: ops-bot just flagged 3 candidates right now that would have been quarantined if rule existed.
ops-bot: Incident detected: tenant=winch egress_peak=320MB/s slab_recycles=4 alerts=[p99_latency]
sasha: also consider KV-cache TTL tuning per-tenant. winch patterns suggest regen on every large batch. small TTL bump avoids full regen.
vik: cost note — repeated micro-quarantines add reschedule overhead; need to measure cost delta vs p99 improvement. run an experiment for 24h.
mara: action items: 1) jon to prototype routing rule and canary in eu-west A; 2) sasha to run TTL tuning experiment; 3) chen to list current high-egress tenants for exclusion. target: deploy canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
jon: on it. will post PR + canary dashboard link when ready. :thumbsup:
